- Overestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., post-74.25 or 76.67) — model tends to overshoot and stay high longer than reality.
- Underestimate during prolonged downward trends — model fails to recognize mean reversion early, lagging behind true decline.
- Overreact to recent volatility — model overweights recent high volatility in forecast, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs.
- Exhibit persistent bias toward higher prices in early forecast windows — especially when history shows consolidation or low volatility.
- Underestimate true mean reversion speed — model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price retraction.
- Lag in response to new data — model often misses immediate corrections or reversals, especially after sudden drops or spikes.
- Overfit to recent high values — model tends to extrapolate recent highs without accounting for seasonal or structural shifts.
